a:
STYLE: 1930s rubber hose cartoon, hand-inked cel animation look, original characters.
Thick uniform outline in dark plum #3D3346 on every shape, clean confident lines, no sketchy strokes.
Flat cel colors with at most one soft shade tone per color, no gradients on characters, no 3D rendering, no glossy plastic look; one small white highlight dot is allowed.
Characters: bendy rubber hose arms and legs with no elbows or knees, white four-finger cartoon gloves, big round shoes, pie-cut eyes (black ovals with a small wedge cut out), simple wide mouth, big head-to-body ratio.
Character colors are saturated: red #D2463C, blue #3E6DB5, yellow #F2C14E, cream #F4E6C8, glove white #FBF6EA.
Backgrounds and large props look like faded watercolor on paper in beige #CFAC8D, sand #D7BE97, dusty navy #4E546E, muted olive #8A9A6B, warm grey #907F77, and are LESS saturated than the characters.
Soft light from the top-left. No cast shadow on the ground. No text, letters or numbers anywhere.
Do not copy any existing cartoon or game character, logo, or scene.

Each item isolated on a flat solid #FF00FF magenta background (or transparent), full figure visible, nothing cropped, wide empty margin around every item, no ground line, no floor, no frame, no border, no shadow under the item.
Characters face the viewer at a slight high 3/4 angle unless a direction is given. "Side" always means facing RIGHT.

RADIO: a boxy old wooden TABLE RADIO, the whole body IS the radio (no human torso).
Rounded-top cabinet in honey wood #B9824F with a cream #F4E6C8 cloth speaker grille on the lower front; the grille is his mouth.
Two round brass tuning DIALS on the upper front are his eyes. One thin metal antenna on top, slightly bent.
Short stiff legs with grey round shoes, rubber hose arms with white gloves, but he holds himself straighter and stiffer than the village characters.
Friendly, eager, a little pushy salesman. About the same height as PIP.

Use case: stylized-concept. Game sprite sheet a, exactly ONE complete character plus his emitted static waves, on pure flat #FF00FF. Landscape canvas, full character at least 600px high. Use attached reference 1 as the primary style anchor, reference 2 only for ink technique, reference 3 for RADIO identity, reference 4 only for horn design (NO horn in this pre-transformation sprite). Show the same rounded-top radio with two dial eyes and grille mouth, but its battery-corrupted cabinet has turned cool grey #9BA3AE and #6E7884, not honey wood in this state. Deliberate battery eye exception: two small glowing dot eyes INSIDE the dark circular dials, NO pie-cut eyes. Straining rigid pose, right-facing side view with both dials readable in a slight three-quarter profile. Bent antenna points to the RIGHT and emits a compact cluster of jagged grey static waves to the RIGHT. No wind-up key or horn yet. Every detached effect within 30px of the antenna or adjacent wave for clean grouping. Wide margins on all sides. No labels, numbers, letters, floor or ground shadow.

RADIO in side view facing RIGHT, straining, antenna pointing forward and shooting jagged grey static waves, dial eyes as two glowing dots, battery-powered stiff body

RADIO REBORN: the same honey-wood table RADIO but reborn by a wind-up key: a brass GRAMOPHONE HORN speaker blooms out of the top of his head like a flower,
a big brass wind-up key turns slowly on his back, gold #F2C14E trim around the cabinet, his two dials became round cheeks and he now has pie-cut eyes above them,
long bouncy rubber hose arms and legs with white gloves and red round shoes. Warm, joyful, full of music. His silhouette must look clearly different from the old stiff RADIO.

Use case: stylized-concept. Game sprite sheet b. Exactly FIVE isolated items on pure flat #FF00FF background. High resolution landscape sheet, approximately 2048x1536, TWO ROWS. Top row THREE evenly spaced full figures: idle, talk, dance. Bottom row TWO items: broadcast in the LEFT two-thirds (allow space for sound on its right), bust portrait in the RIGHT third. Leave broad empty gutters between every item and row. Every full character at least 500px tall. Do NOT include sixth item or empty-cell markers. Reference 1 is primary style anchor; reference 2 is ink technique only (never copy its character/text); reference 3 is the radio identity before transformation; reference 4 is flower-shaped brass horn reference ONLY, not its moustache or cabinet. All five items share exactly the same reborn design: rounded-top honey-wood tabletop radio cabinet, cream smiling cloth grille below, round brass dial CHEEKS below two separate large PIE-CUT EYES, big flowering brass gramophone horn above, visibly protruding twin-loop brass WIND-UP KEY on back, long sinuous rubber hose limbs, white gloves, red round shoes. Not a gramophone grandfather: NO moustache. Cabinet is entire body, no separate torso/head. Flat cel fills, plum outlines, simple clean shapes legible at 140px. First three poses front/slight high three-quarter. Fourth pose is right-facing SIDE VIEW braced wide, horn aimed RIGHT, strong compact rightward stream of several warm gold outlined sound rings and music notes. Keep detached musical shapes within 30px of their parent cluster so slicing attaches them to the right character; none cross cell gutters. Fifth item is a self-contained close bust with full horn and cabinet face, no legs, no surrounding frame. No ground shadows, no text, no labels, no grid lines. Read order is top left to right, then bottom left to right.
